about: Wonders (the Ledger topic 'Buildings and works': 'The Seven Wonders and a list across all ages'). Each stands once in the world, at its place (lon, lat). 'builder' is the realm that built it in history (a civilization key); only that realm builds it among the others, from 'start', in the years history took (to 'done'), if it holds the place. You may build any of them from history's 'start', in any of your provinces, and so take it first. It falls in 'fall' as history had ('fall_why'); only yours can be saved. Costs: talents, workers (men taken from your manpower while it is built) and special goods your realm must have. Effects apply to the realm holding it; 'culture' adds to the score. Dates from the standard histories. Our own data, free for any use.

wonders.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
wonders.description: The oldest of the Seven Wonders, and the only one still standing.

wonders.name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
wonders.fall_why: gone, unrecorded, by the first century
wonders.description: Terraced gardens watered from the Euphrates, told of by Berossus and Strabo.

wonders.name: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
wonders.fall_why: burnt by the Goths in AD 262
wonders.description: Rebuilt after Herostratus burnt it in 356 BC; pilgrims and bankers crowd it.

wonders.name: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
wonders.fall_why: carried to Constantinople and lost in the fire of AD 475
wonders.description: Phidias' gold and ivory Zeus, enthroned in his temple at Olympia.

wonders.name: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
wonders.fall_why: thrown down by earthquakes; the Knights took its stones in 1404
wonders.description: The tomb of Mausolus, whose name every great tomb now bears.

wonders.name: Colossus of Rhodes
wonders.fall_why: thrown down by the earthquake of 226 BC
wonders.description: A bronze Helios at the harbour, paid for with the siege engines Demetrius left behind.

wonders.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
wonders.fall_why: broken by the earthquakes of 1303 and 1323
wonders.description: The Pharos guides ships to the greatest harbour of the age: sea travel is cheaper.

wonders.name: Library of Alexandria
wonders.fall_why: ruined when Aurelian took Alexandria in AD 272
wonders.description: Every book the Ptolemies could buy or copy: research grows by a quarter.

wonders.name: Serapeum of Alexandria
wonders.description: Ptolemy III's temple to Serapis, the god he gave Greeks and Egyptians alike.

wonders.name: Great Altar of Pergamon
wonders.description: The Attalids' altar to Zeus, its frieze the war of gods and giants.

wonders.name: Mausoleum of Augustus
wonders.description: The first emperor's tomb on the Campus Martius.

wonders.name: Herod's Temple
wonders.fall_why: burnt by Titus' army in AD 70
wonders.description: Herod's rebuilding of the Temple at Jerusalem, the greatest in the east.

wonders.name: Temple of Jupiter at Baalbek
wonders.description: The largest temple of the Roman world, on stones no one else could move.

wonders.name: The Treasury at Petra
wonders.description: Carved from the rose-red rock of the Nabataeans' caravan city.

wonders.name: Temple of Bel at Palmyra
wonders.description: The great temple of Palmyra, where the caravan roads met.

wonders.name: Colosseum
wonders.description: The Flavian amphitheatre: 50,000 Romans watch the games.

wonders.name: Trajan's Forum and Column
wonders.description: Paid for with the gold of Dacia; the column tells the war.

wonders.name: Pantheon
wonders.description: Hadrian's temple of all the gods, its dome unmatched for 1,300 years.

wonders.name: Baths of Caracalla
wonders.fall_why: dry once the Goths cut the aqueducts in AD 537
wonders.description: Baths for 1,600 bathers at once.

wonders.name: Theodosian Walls
wonders.description: The land walls of Constantinople, unbroken for a thousand years.

wonders.name: Hagia Sophia
wonders.description: Justinian's church, its dome 'hung from heaven by a golden chain'.

wonders.name: Dome of the Rock
wonders.description: Abd al-Malik's shrine on the Temple Mount.

wonders.name: Great Mosque of Damascus
wonders.description: The Umayyads' mosque, walls of gold mosaic.

wonders.name: Great Mosque of Cordoba
wonders.description: A forest of red and white arches, grown over two centuries.

wonders.name: Palatine Chapel at Aachen
wonders.description: Charlemagne's chapel, built with columns taken from Ravenna and Rome.

wonders.name: St Mark's Basilica
wonders.description: Venice's church of the Evangelist, its gold won by trade and the Fourth Crusade.

wonders.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
wonders.description: The great Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité.

wonders.name: Chartres Cathedral
wonders.description: Its windows tell the whole of scripture in blue glass.

wonders.name: Alhambra
wonders.description: The Nasrids' red palace above Granada.

wonders.name: Florence Cathedral dome
wonders.description: Brunelleschi's dome, raised without centring.

wonders.name: Topkapi Palace
wonders.description: The Ottoman sultans' palace and the seat of their government.

wonders.name: St Peter's Basilica
wonders.description: The largest church in Christendom, over a century of building.

wonders.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
wonders.description: Sinan's mosque for Suleiman, with its schools, hospital and library.

wonders.name: El Escorial
wonders.description: Philip II's palace, monastery and library.

wonders.name: Palace of Versailles
wonders.description: Louis XIV's court, where the nobles were kept close.

wonders.name: St Paul's Cathedral
wonders.description: Wren's cathedral, risen from the Great Fire.

wonders.name: Palace of Westminster
wonders.description: The Houses of Parliament, rebuilt after the fire of 1834.

wonders.name: Eiffel Tower
wonders.description: Built for the World's Fair of 1889, the tallest thing made by hand.
